text: A survey of 12,000 under-40 office workers found an 11-point blood pressure drop, only among those cutting salt.
Coffee improved memory by 2 percent in university students after a sleepless night, on one word-list test.
Working from home raised productivity in three start-ups' software teams, but self-reported gains vanished after six months.
The new bridge saved bus passengers about twenty minutes on average, compared with a year of roadworks.
Vitamin D may prevent colds, a benefit seen only in under-fives in one supplement-maker-funded winter trial.
A reading app helped children learning English as a second language, though gains faded by the next school year.
A pesticide study in two English counties found bumblebee colonies produced a quarter fewer queens in one season.
A four-day week in Icelandic public offices reduced burnout, with pay unchanged and no change in sick days.
